mainTopic: Whether women are commanded in פרו ורבו; the end of פרק הבא על יבמתו; and the opening of פרק אלמנה לכהן גדול: why a forbidden wife's עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה.
overview: The amud opens with the last word of a story about the twin daughters of רבי חייא's wife. The גמרא then asks whether women are really exempt from פרו ורבו, pointing to a case where the court forced a master to free a half-slave woman. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that she was freed because men were treating her loosely. The chapter הבא על יבמתו then ends, and the chapter אלמנה לכהן גדול begins. Its משנה rules that when a woman is in a forbidden marriage to a כהן, her עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה, but her עבדי צאן ברזל do. In a valid marriage all her slaves eat, and a בת כהן married to a ישראל loses תרומה for all her slaves. The גמרא asks why the עבדי מלוג should not eat as 'his acquisition that acquired an acquisition.' It gives three answers: רבינא's rule that only a קנין who eats can let others eat, רבא's rabbinic decree meant to push toward divorce, and רב אשי's decree aimed at a כהנת widow who might wrongly think she can go back to her father's תרומה. The amud ends by opening a new question about appraised property (שום), and רב יהודה's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the story: the twins were sisters
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the earlier story about the twin children of רבי חייא's wife: the twin daughters were sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...were sisters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began just before this section, about the twins born to רבי חייא's wife יהודית. This one word tells us that the twins being described were sisters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line closes the story that led to the earlier claim that women are not commanded in פרו ורבו. That claim is exactly what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: sisters

phrases.english: were sisters.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a story told just before here, about the twin daughters of רבי חייא's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative detail: the twin daughters were sisters.

steps.title: Are women really not commanded to have children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that women are not commanded in פרו ורבו. Its proof is a case where the court forced a master to free a half-slave woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are women not commanded? But רב אחא בר רב קטינא said in the name of רבי יצחק: There was a case of a woman who was half slave and half free. The court forced her master, and he set her free!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that women have no מצוה of having children. It brings a story where the court forced a master to free a half-slave woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A half-slave, half-free woman cannot marry a Jew and cannot marry a slave, so she can never have children in a permitted way. If the court forced her master to free her, it seems the reason was so she could marry and have children. That would mean women are commanded in פרו ורבו.

keyTerms.meaning: they are commanded
half slave and half free woman
they forced (the court compelled)
her master
but didn't (so-and-so) say? (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבה means 'her master' (the slave's owner), not the אמורא named רבה.

phrases.english: And are they not commanded?
phrases.notes: 'They' means women, and the מצוה meant is having children (פרו ורבו).

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Acha bar Rav Ketina say
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
There was an incident with a certain woman
who was half slave and half free woman,
and they forced her master
and he made her a free woman!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִיפַּקְדִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier claim, tied to the story just finished, that women are not commanded in פרו ורבו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that women are not commanded in פרו ורבו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The court forced the freeing of a half-slave woman. The only clear reason seems to be letting her marry and have children, which implies women have that מצוה.

steps.title: She was freed because of improper conduct
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the court forced her freedom because men were treating her loosely, not because of a מצוה to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: People were treating her as ownerless, behaving loosely with her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge. The court freed her to stop improper behavior, not because she had a מצוה to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She could not marry anyone, so men were acting loosely with her. Freeing her let her marry and stopped this sinful behavior. Because the case has a different reason, it no longer proves that women are commanded in פרו ורבו.

keyTerms.meaning: ownerless (loose) behavior
they treated her

steps.whatToRemember: The half-slave case does not prove women are commanded in פרו ורבו. The court freed her to stop improper behavior.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
They treated her in an ownerless (loose) manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִנְהַג הֶפְקֵר נָהֲגוּ בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling in the cited case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court freed her so she could fulfill פרו ורבו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court freed her to stop immoral behavior. Women may still be exempt from פרו ורבו.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הבא על יבמתו
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marks the end of the chapter הבא על יבמתו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הבא על יבמתו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the formal closing line for the chapter הבא על יבמתו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן says we will come back to learn this chapter again. A new chapter starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (chapter-closing formula)

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'One who has relations with his yevama'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter הבא על יבמתו is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: which slaves of a forbidden wife eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter's משנה covers a woman in a forbidden marriage to a כהן who brings slaves into the marriage. עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה, but עבדי צאן ברזל do.
steps.simpleTranslation: A widow married to a כהן גדול, or a divorcée or חלוצה married to an ordinary כהן, brought him slaves of מלוג and slaves of צאן ברזל. The מלוג slaves do not eat תרומה. The צאן ברזל slaves do eat.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It asks whether slaves that a wife brings to a כהן can eat תרומה when the marriage itself is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These marriages are forbidden by the Torah, so the woman herself does not gain the right to eat תרומה through her husband. Her slaves are different. עבדי מלוג still belong to her, so they do not eat. עבדי צאן ברזל count as the husband's property, so they eat as slaves owned by a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: slaves of usufruct: the wife owns them, and the husband only uses them and keeps their earnings
slaves of 'iron sheep': the husband takes responsibility for their value, so they count as his
an ordinary כהן
a woman released from יבום through חליצה
the holy produce given to כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds of slaves come from the wife. What decides the din is who carries the risk if their value goes up or down: she does for מלוג, he does for צאן ברזל.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a slave eats תרומה because a כהן owns him, even when the marriage that brought the slave is forbidden.

phrases.english: A widow married to a High Priest,
a divorcée or a chalutza married to an ordinary priest,
if she brought him slaves of usufruct (melog)
and slaves of guaranteed investment (tzon barzel),
the melog slaves do not eat teruma,
the tzon barzel slaves do eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, גְּרוּשָׁה וַחֲלוּצָה לְכֹהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a forbidden marriage to a כהן, the wife's עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה, but her עבדי צאן ברזל do.

steps.title: Defining the two kinds of slaves a wife brings in
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines עבדי מלוג as slaves whose loss and gain belong to the wife. Even though the husband must feed them, they do not eat תרומה. עבדי צאן ברזל are slaves whose loss and gain belong to the husband. Since he is responsible for them, they eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are עבדי מלוג: if they die, it is her loss, and if they go up in value, it is her gain. Even though he must feed them, they do not eat תרומה. These are עבדי צאן ברזל: if they die, it is his loss, and if they go up in value, it is his gain. Since he is responsible for them, they eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is explaining the two terms it used in the previous step, so we know exactly which slaves eat תרומה in the forbidden-marriage case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is who carries the risk and the profit. Feeding the slaves is not enough to count them as the כהן's. Being responsible for their value (אחריות) makes them count as his property, so they eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaves who stay the wife's property; the husband only gets the use of them
'Iron flock' slaves; the husband takes full responsibility for their value
They increased (went up in value)
Their food and support
Responsibility for them (for any loss)

phrases.english: And these are the slaves of מלוג:
if they die, they die to her (her loss),
and if they increase in value, they increase for her;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב בִּמְזוֹנוֹתָן
phrases.english: even though he is obligated to feed them,
these do not eat תרומה.
And these are the slaves of צאן ברזל:
if they die, they die to him (his loss),
and if they increase in value, they increase for him;
since he is responsible for them,
these eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two terms from the משנה's ruling in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Responsibility for loss and gain decides ownership. In a forbidden marriage, עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה and עבדי צאן ברזל do.

steps.title: Valid marriages: a ישראל woman to a כהן, and a כהן's daughter to a ישראל
steps.stepSummary: When a בת ישראל validly marries a כהן, both kinds of slaves she brings eat תרומה. When a בת כהן marries a ישראל, neither kind eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל woman who married a כהן and brought slaves into the marriage: whether they are עבדי מלוג or עבדי צאן ברזל, they eat תרומה. A כהן's daughter who married a ישראל and brought slaves into the marriage: whether they are עבדי מלוג or עבדי צאן ברזל, they do not eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more cases, both valid marriages. Here the type of slave does not matter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the marriage is valid, the wife herself eats תרומה as a כהן's wife, so all her slaves eat too. A בת כהן who marries a ישראל loses her right to תרומה, so even slaves she brought from her father's house stop eating.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from a non-כהן family
A daughter of a כהן
She brought in to him (into the marriage)
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their household may eat

steps.whatToRemember: In a valid marriage to a כהן, all her slaves eat. In a forbidden marriage, only עבדי צאן ברזל eat. A בת כהן married to a ישראל: none of her slaves eat.

phrases.english: A ישראל woman who married a כהן
and brought slaves into the marriage for him,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עַבְדֵי מְלוֹג, בֵּין עַבְדֵי צֹאן בַּרְזֶל —
phrases.english: whether slaves of מלוג or slaves of צאן ברזל,
these eat תרומה.
And a כהן's daughter who married a ישראל
and brought slaves into the marriage for him,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין עַבְדֵי מְלוֹג, בֵּין עַבְדֵי צֹאן בַּרְזֶל —
phrases.english: whether slaves of מלוג or slaves of צאן ברזל,
these do not eat תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְכֹהֵן וְהִכְנִיסָה לוֹ עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds valid-marriage cases to contrast with the forbidden-marriage case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a valid marriage to a כהן, all slaves she brings eat תרומה. A בת כהן married to a ישראל: none of her slaves eat.

steps.title: Why shouldn't the wife's מלוג slaves eat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that עבדי מלוג do not eat in a forbidden marriage. They should count as 'his acquisition that acquired an acquisition'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה — why not? Let them be like 'his acquisition that acquired an acquisition'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by attacking the משנה's ruling in step 5 and step 6 about עבדי מלוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife is the כהן's 'acquisition', and her slaves are her acquisition. So they should eat through her, even though the husband does not own them outright. The source for this rule comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why?
His acquisition that acquired an acquisition

steps.confusionAlert: The question is only about the forbidden marriage from step 5. In a valid marriage the משנה already said all her slaves eat.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And the slaves of מלוג
do not eat תרומה — why?
Let them be like his acquisition that acquired an acquisition!
phrases.notes: The wife counts as the כהן's acquisition, and her slaves are what she acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַבְדֵי מְלוֹג לֹא יֹאכְלוּ בִּתְרוּמָה, אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling on עבדי מלוג
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that עבדי מלוג do not eat תרומה in a forbidden marriage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of קנינו שקנה קנין says that what a כהן's acquisition acquires also eats. The wife is his acquisition, so her slaves should eat.

steps.title: The ברייתא source: a כהן's acquisition that acquires also eats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its challenge. It learns from the פסוק 'קנין כספו הוא יאכל בו' that a כהן's slaves eat. It also learns that slaves acquired by his wife, or by his own slaves, eat as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: From where do we know that a כהן who married a woman and acquired slaves, they eat תרומה? The פסוק says: 'And if a כהן acquires a person, the purchase of his money, he may eat of it.' And from where do we know that a wife who acquired slaves, and his slaves who acquired slaves, they eat תרומה? The same פסוק says it. It teaches that if his acquisition acquired an acquisition, that one also eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the source behind its challenge. The next step answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the same פסוק twice. First it teaches that a כהן's slaves eat. Then it teaches the extra layer: what his wife or his slaves acquire also eats. This seems to prove that the wife's עבדי מלוג should eat, which makes the משנה hard to understand.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
As it is said (in a פסוק)
The purchase of his money

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where do we know regarding a כהן who married a woman
and acquired slaves, that they eat תרומה?
As it is said: 'And if a כהן acquires a person,
the purchase of his money, he may eat of it.'
And from where do we know regarding a wife who acquired slaves,
and his slaves who acquired slaves,
that they eat תרומה?
As it is said: 'And if a כהן acquires a person,
the purchase of his money, he may eat of it,'
his acquisition that acquired an acquisition eats.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא reads the same פסוק a second time to teach this extra layer: even someone bought by his acquisition can eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מִנַּיִן לְכֹהֵן שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה וְקָנָה עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ברייתא source behind the challenge in step 8
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that the wife's עבדי מלוג should eat תרומה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 22:11: what a כהן's wife or slaves acquire also eats תרומה

steps.title: Whoever eats can let others eat; whoever does not eat cannot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8 with a rule: only someone who eats תרומה can let others eat. The forbidden wife does not eat, so her slaves cannot eat through her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who eats תרומה can let others eat. Anyone who does not eat cannot let others eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from steps 8 and 9 about why the forbidden wife's slaves don't eat. The wife herself does not eat תרומה, so she has no power to pass eating on to her slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that a קנין of a קנין eats. But the middle link here is the wife, and she is barred from תרומה because the marriage is forbidden. A link that cannot eat cannot pass the right to eat down to anyone else, so the chain breaks.

keyTerms.meaning: one who eats (here: eats תרומה)
one who lets others eat (gives them the right to eat תרומה)
does not let others eat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up אוכל (he eats) and מאכיל (he lets others eat). The whole sugya is about whether someone who cannot eat can still give that right to others.

phrases.english: Whoever eats [תרומה] lets others eat;
whoever does not eat does not let others eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8, which step 9 backed up with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces a limiting principle: the middle link must itself be able to eat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any קנין of a קנין eats, so the forbidden wife's slaves should eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wife cannot eat, so she cannot let her slaves eat.

steps.title: Challenge from an uncircumcised כהן and impure כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule. An ערל כהן and a טמא כהן do not eat תרומה, yet they let their wives and slaves eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? An uncircumcised כהן and all impure כהנים do not eat, yet they let others eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 10. It finds cases where a person does not eat תרומה but still lets others eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ערל or a טמא כהן is not allowed to eat תרומה, yet his wife and slaves do eat. That seems to break the rule that 'whoever does not eat cannot let others eat.'

keyTerms.meaning: an uncircumcised man (here, a כהן who is barred from תרומה)
people who are ritually impure
but look at the case of... (introduces a counterexample)

phrases.english: And does one who does not eat really not let others eat? But look at an uncircumcised [כהן],
and all the impure [כהנים],
who do not eat, yet they let others eat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just stated in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'whoever does not eat does not let others eat'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: the ערל and the טמא do not eat, yet their households do.

steps.title: Their mouths simply hurt
steps.stepSummary: The ערל and the טמא are still fully fit to eat. Something is just temporarily stopping them, like a sore mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is as if their mouths hurt them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ערל and the טמא are not truly unfit for תרומה; they are only held back for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of non-eaters. Some are blocked by who they are, and some are only blocked by a passing obstacle. The ערל and the טמא keep their basic right to eat, the way a man with a sore mouth still owns his food, so they can still let others eat. The forbidden wife is truly unfit, so the rule still applies to her.

keyTerms.meaning: there (in that case)
their mouth hurts them (only a temporary obstacle)

phrases.english: There, their mouths hurt them.
phrases.notes: A picture: they really have the right to eat. Something outside is just stopping them for now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: a temporary obstacle versus being truly unfit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any non-eater who lets others eat breaks the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערל and the טמא are fit to eat and only blocked for now, so they still let others eat.

steps.title: Challenge from a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: A ממזר is truly unfit to eat תרומה. Yet a ממזר grandchild lets his grandmother keep eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a ממזר, who does not eat, yet lets others eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a harder counterexample. This time the person is truly unfit, not just temporarily blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Take a בת ישראל who had a child with a כהן and was later widowed. Her child married a ממזר and had a child, and then her own child died. This ממזר grandchild still lets her eat תרומה, because she has a living descendant from the כהן. He cannot eat himself, so the 'sore mouth' answer from step 12 doesn't work here.

keyTerms.meaning: a child born from a forbidden relationship; truly unfit for תרומה

phrases.english: But look at a ממזר,
who does not eat, yet lets others eat!
phrases.notes: He lets his grandmother keep eating, because she has a living descendant from the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 12's answer, the גמרא brings a counterexample that answer cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule 'whoever does not eat does not let others eat' (from step 10).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ממזר is truly unfit, not just held back, yet he still lets his grandmother eat.

steps.title: רבינא: the rule is about a קנין
steps.stepSummary: רבינא narrows the rule so it only covers a קנין, someone the כהן acquired. A קנין who eats lets others eat; a קנין who does not eat cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The rule is speaking about a קנין who eats. A קנין who eats lets others eat. One who does not eat does not let others eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the ממזר challenge. He explains that the rule from step 10 was only ever talking about people the כהן acquired.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממזר is not the כהן's קנין. He is a descendant, and he helps the grandmother through a different path. The forbidden wife is the כהן's קנין, so the rule applies to her. Since she cannot eat, her slaves cannot eat through her.

keyTerms.meaning: an acquisition (someone acquired by the כהן, like a wife or a slave)
he is saying / he is referring to

steps.whatToRemember: Only a קנין of the כהן who can eat passes the right to eat on to others. The forbidden wife is a קנין who cannot eat, so her עבדי מלוג do not eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the משנה's ruling about עבדי מלוג from step 5. It also shows that a descendant like the ממזר works through a different path than a קנין.

phrases.english: רבינא said:
It is speaking about a קנין who eats:
phrases.notes: He means someone the כהן acquired, like a wife or a slave, not a child or grandchild.

phrases.english: a קנין who eats lets others eat;
one who does not eat does not let others eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ממזר challenge of step 13 by narrowing the rule from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: the rule covers only a קנין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers everyone, so the ממזר contradicts it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only a קנין. The ממזר is a descendant, not a קנין, so he is outside the rule.

steps.title: רבא: Torah allows it, but the רבנן stopped it to push toward divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the slaves may eat תרומה by Torah law, but the רבנן forbade it. That way the wife will complain, and the husband will end up divorcing her.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: By Torah law they do eat. It is the רבנן who made a decree against them. They did it so she will say: 'I don't eat, and my slaves don't eat. Am I just a harlot to him?!' Because of this, he will end up divorcing her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a completely different reason why the forbidden wife's slaves do not eat תרומה. He says it is only a rabbinic decree, made to push the couple apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10-14 tried to explain the law with a Torah-level rule about who lets others eat. רבא drops that whole approach. He says the Torah does let the slaves eat, and the ban is a rabbinic tool. Being shut out of תרומה will embarrass the wife and lead to the forbidden marriage ending.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
They (the רבנן) made a decree
A woman in a forbidden, illicit relationship
To send her out, meaning to divorce her

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the slaves are unfit by Torah law. By Torah law they may eat; only the רבנן forbade it, and on purpose.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
By Torah law, they do eat,
phrases.notes: "They" means the slaves of the forbidden wife, the ones we have been discussing.

phrases.english: and it is the Rabbis who made a decree against them,
so that she will say:
I do not eat,
my slaves do not eat —
am I a harlot to him?!
Therefore he will come to divorce her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation instead of the rule refined by רבינא in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the law as a rabbinic decree with a social purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaves are blocked by Torah law because their owner does not eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law the slaves eat. The ban is rabbinic, meant to lead to a divorce.

steps.title: רב אשי: a decree so she won't feed them after her husband dies
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ban is a rabbinic decree. Otherwise she might keep feeding the slaves תרומה even after the כהן dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is a decree, in case she lets them eat after death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a third explanation. The רבנן forbade the slaves now so that she will not keep feeding them after her husband dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the כהן is alive, she counts as his, so her slaves may eat through her. Once he dies, that link is gone and they may no longer eat. The worry is that she will not notice this change and will keep feeding them, so the רבנן stopped it from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Lest; in case
After (her husband's) death

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is a decree, lest she let them eat
after death.
phrases.notes: He means after her husband, the כהן, dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא תַּאֲכִיל לְאַחַר מִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative explanation, alongside רבא's in step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaves are blocked now so they will not keep eating after the husband dies.

steps.title: Then every בת ישראל married to a כהן should be included
steps.stepSummary: If that were the reason, then any בת ישראל married to a כהן should also be barred from feeding her slaves תרומה, for the same worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a בת ישראל who married a כהן should not let them eat either! It should be a decree, in case she lets them eat after death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's reason. It shows that the reason would apply far too broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear of eating after death applies to every בת ישראל married to a כהן. She also loses the right when her husband dies. Yet she does feed her slaves תרומה during the marriage, so this fear cannot be the reason for the ban.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so (a phrase that opens a challenge)
A woman who is not from a כהן's family
Who married

phrases.english: But if so,
an Israelite woman who married a Kohen
should not let them eat,
as a decree, lest she let them eat
after death!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן לֹא תַּאֲכִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's decree from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reason: a decree in case she feeds them after death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason proves too much. It would forbid every בת ישראל married to a כהן, which is not the law.

steps.title: רב אשי refines: the worry is a כהן's daughter who thinks she can go back
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי narrows his decree to a widow who is a כהנת. She might reason that after her husband dies she can go back to eating in her father's house. She does not realize that this forbidden marriage made her a חללה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: It is about a widow who is a כהן's daughter. She might come to reason: 'At first, my slaves ate the תרומה of my father's house. I married this man, and they ate my husband's תרומה. Now I have gone back to my original status.' She does not realize that at first she had not made herself a חללה, but now she has made herself a חללה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge by saying his decree is really about a specific case: a כהן's daughter. Her special mistake is what the רבנן were worried about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain בת ישראל knows that once her husband dies she has nothing to go back to, so there is no risk. A כהנת might think she simply returns to her father's תרומה. But marrying the כהן גדול when it was forbidden made her a חללה, so she has lost that right forever. To prevent that mistake, the רבנן blocked the slaves from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow who is the daughter of a כהן
To rule for herself; to reason her way to a decision
Her father's house
A woman disqualified from כהונה through a forbidden relationship with a כהן
My original status

steps.whatToRemember: There are three reasons the slaves of the forbidden wife do not eat. רבינא: only a קנין who eats lets others eat. רבא: a rabbinic decree to push toward divorce. רב אשי: a decree so a כהנת widow will not mistakenly go back to her father's תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: The mistake she makes is about herself, not her husband. Her own forbidden marriage turned her into a חללה, so her father's house can no longer feed her or her slaves.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
It is about a widow who is a Kohen's daughter,
who will come to reason for herself:
At first, [my slaves] ate
the teruma of my father's house,
I married this man —
and they ate the teruma of my husband,
and now I have gone back
to my original situation.
And she does not realize
that at first she had not made herself a ḥalala,
but now she has made herself a ḥalala.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: בְּאַלְמָנָה כֹּהֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by limiting רב אשי's decree to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to explain why the decree is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree is a general worry about any wife feeding slaves after her husband's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree targets a כהנת widow, who might wrongly think she can return to her father's תרומה.

steps.title: What about a widow who is a בת ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's narrowed reason. It works for a widow who is a כהנת, but it does not seem to fit a widow who is a בת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works out for a widow who is a כהנת. But for a widow who is a בת ישראל, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap in רב אשי's answer from Step 18. His reason only fits a widow who comes from a כהן family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said the ban exists because a כהנת widow might think she can go back to eating תרומה in her father's house. A בת ישראל never ate תרומה in her father's house, so she could never make that mistake. So why should the ban apply to her?

keyTerms.meaning: It works out / that is fine (for this case)
A widow who is the daughter of a כהן
A widow who is the daughter of a regular Jew, not a כהן
What can be said? (the case is not explained)

phrases.english: It works out for a widow who is a כהנת,
phrases.notes: This refers to רב אשי's reason in the last step: she might think she can go back to eating in her father's house.

phrases.english: but a widow who is a בת ישראל,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח אַלְמָנָה כֹּהֶנֶת, אַלְמָנָה בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed version of רב אשי's decree from Step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reason that the decree is limited to a כהנת widow who might think she returns to her father's house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ban also applies to a בת ישראל widow, but she has no father's house where she ate תרומה, so the stated reason does not cover her.

steps.title: The רבנן made one rule for all widows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that when it comes to widows, the רבנן did not make a distinction. They decreed for every widow, even the ones the worry does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it comes to her being a widow, the רבנן did not make a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the רבנן made one blanket rule for all widows married to a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry really comes from the כהנת widow. But the רבנן did not want separate rules for different kinds of widows, so the decree covers the בת ישראל widow too. Her case is included in the rule even though the reason does not fit her exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Her being a widow
The רבנן did not make a distinction (between cases)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's reason holds: the ban is a rabbinic decree driven by the כהנת widow's mistake, and the רבנן applied it to every widow without making exceptions.
steps.confusionAlert: Here לָא פְּלִיגִי does not mean 'they did not argue with each other.' It means the רבנן did not split the rule into different cases.

phrases.english: Regarding her widowhood, the Rabbis did not distinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Blanket decree (לא פלוג): the rabbinic rule is applied the same way to all widows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the worry only fits a כהנת widow, a בת ישראל widow should be allowed to feed her slaves תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן made one rule for all widows, so the בת ישראל widow is included in the ban as well

steps.title: Items back or their value? A new question about appraised property
steps.stepSummary: A new discussion begins. A wife brought appraised property (שום) into the marriage. When the marriage ends, she wants the actual items and he wants to pay their value. Who is right? רב יהודה's answer is introduced here.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A woman brings appraised property into the marriage. She says, 'I am taking my items,' and he says, 'I am giving you their money value.' Whom does the law favor? רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a disagreement between the wife and her husband. It also sets up רב יהודה's answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Property marked as שום was valued and written into the כתובה, and the husband takes responsibility for that value. Because he guarantees its value, he claims he only owes her money. She claims the items are still hers, so she should get them back.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who brings (property) into the marriage
Appraised property, valued and written into the כתובה with the husband guaranteeing it
Money value
Whom does the law favor?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at 'רב יהודה said'. His actual ruling has not been given yet. It comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: It was stated: A woman who brings appraised property into her husband's possession,
she says: I am taking my items,
and he says: I am giving their money value,
whom does the law favor?
רב יהודה said:
phrases.notes: His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the משנה's discussion of property the wife brings into the marriage
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When a marriage ends, does a wife get back the actual appraised items she brought in, or may the husband pay her their value instead?
